conventions.convention: The background is a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold of signature (-,+,+,+), the scalar is smooth and real, and Countable Choice is retained for the smooth tangent-bundle conventions.
J_a^X = Q_ab X^b is the multiplier covector, while the energy-current vector is j_X^a = -g^{ab}J_b^X. Its flux through a spacelike face oriented with future adapted unit normal n has density Q(n,X).
The Schwarzschild extension has orientation dv ∧ dr ∧ ω_S²; its horizon contribution uses the positive measure s² dv dΩ and the inner outward boundary orientation.

K_delta includes the whole sphere factor, with |r-3s/2| ≤ delta and 0 < delta < s/2. The proposed estimate integrates the full stationary first-derivative energy in the length coordinate x⁰, with one constant independent of the wave.
Kerr horizon modes satisfy Tu = -iωu and Φu = imu, with m an integer and shifted frequency ω̃ = ω-mΩ_H. These are local trace data and need not extend to global wave solutions.

The horizon average follows the stationary field T for a full period 2π/ω, entirely inside the mode patch. Strict negativity is asserted only where the trace is nonzero, or on admissible spacelike cut patches meeting its nonzero set.
In the concentration proof only, t denotes x⁰, the length coordinate, rather than the physical time x⁰/c. Frequency may depend on the prescribed finite concentration interval.

load_bearing.statement: Q_ab[ψ] = (∇_aψ)(∇_bψ) - (1/2)g_ab g^{cd}(∇_cψ)(∇_dψ), J_a^X[ψ] = Q_ab[ψ]X^b, and j_X^a[ψ] = -g^{ab}J_b^X[ψ], for a smooth real scalar on a fixed smooth Lorentzian background.

Assuming Countable Choice, for every H > 0 and 0 < ε < 1 there is a globally smooth real Schwarzschild scalar wave with compact smooth initial data, E_T(0) = 1, and E_{T,delta}(x⁰) ≥ 1-ε for every 0 ≤ x⁰ ≤ H. Its stationary energy is one on every static slice.
Assuming Countable Choice, for a future unit timelike n, future causal X, and smooth real scalar, Q(n,n) = (a²+|b|²)/2 and Q(n,X) ≥ 0, where a = dψ(n) and b = h_n(sharp_g(dψ)).
∇^aJ_a^X[ψ] = (Box_g ψ)X^b∇_bψ + (1/2)Q^{ab}[ψ](L_Xg)_ab. Consequently the multiplier current has zero divergence for a wave solution and a Killing multiplier.

A nondegenerate integrated local energy estimate with no trapping loss on K_delta means that one finite constant C, independent of ψ, bounds the integral from zero to infinity of E_{T,delta}[ψ](x⁰) by C E_T[ψ](0) for every smooth finite-initial-energy wave.

For the stated smooth Kerr horizon mode trace with ω > 0 and an admissible full stationary-period segment, the averaged density is (1/2)ω(ω-mΩ_H)|u|². In the band mΩ_H > ω > 0 it is strictly negative exactly off the nodes; its integral on an admissible compact spacelike cut patch is negative whenever the restricted trace is not identically zero.

The background connection, inverse-metric contractions, and geometric conventions referenced by the scalar definition.
The definition L_Xg = 0 for Killing multipliers.
Torsion freedom, metric compatibility, the tensor product rule, and the Christoffel formula.
The identity (L_Xg)_ab = ∇_aX_b + ∇_bX_a; no Hilbert-action conservation hypothesis is imported into the test-scalar argument.
Timelike and null causal classification, including exclusion of zero from the defined causal class.
Future unit timelike observers, rest spaces, and h_n(v) = v+g(n,v)n.
Orthogonal observer decomposition and positivity of the metric on n-perpendicular.
The rest-space estimate |g(b,Y)| ≤ |b||Y| in the dominant-energy proof.
Current three-forms, finite smooth singular chains, adapted normals, and orientation-sensitive flux.
Finite-chain Stokes balance and the non-null face formula with factor ε g(j,ν).
The fixed exterior metric, s > 0, f = 1-s/r, product sphere structure, and length coordinate x⁰.
Global Lorentzian signature and the future timelike stationary field on r > s.
The smooth advanced metric across r = s, its compatible time orientation, and the null generator ∂_v.
The future circular null geodesic at r = 3s/2 and its traversal of every static time slice.
A smooth radial cutoff supported strictly inside the specified annulus.
The stationary orbit equation γ′ = T used in the averaging definition.
The maximal stationary integral curve through each horizon point.
Smooth dependence over a compact stationary orbit segment, ensuring nearby admissible averaging points.

concerns.concern: Proof step 1.1 writes Q(n,n) = a² - (1/2)(-a²+|b|²) = (a²+|b|²)/2. The first equality has the wrong sign: g(n,n) = -1 gives a² + (1/2)(-a²+|b|²). The stated conclusion and the subsequent dominant-energy argument are correct after this immediate correction.

Proof step 4.2 says Taylor's theorem 'bounds the last parenthesis by C|x|³', immediately after displaying h^{-2}(V_0(x)-Ω²+Ω⁴x²)a. The unscaled Taylor remainder V_0(x)-Ω²+Ω⁴x² has that bound; the h^{-2}-scaled expression does not have it uniformly in h. The following norm calculation correctly retains h^{-2} and obtains O_H(sqrt(h)), so this is a wording defect rather than a failure of the residual estimate.

The mode definition and flux lemma preserve the regular ingoing extension, compatible future orientation, χ = T+Ω_HΦ, and Ω_H = a/(r_+²+a²). Their restriction to 0 < |a| < M is legitimate. The supplier's stationary-limit diagram agrees with its radius formula; no diagram occurs in the assigned items.
